correctness.rationale: For X_m: xy=z^m (odd m≥3,char k≠2), the hypersurface Gauss map is the blowup of its Jacobian gradient ideal. In wild char dividing m the ideal is (x,y), otherwise (x,y,z^{m−1}); this follows from the literal derivatives (y,x,−mz^{m−1}). On the generic exceptional chart t=y/x invertible, the wild Rees chart has tx²=z^m, while tame adding u=z^{m−1}/x eliminates to u²=t z^{m−2}, x=zu/t. Both charts embed into the same function field. With s²=tz, the local generic one-dimensional rings over K=k(t) have valuations generated by <2,m> and <2,m−2>. For odd r the absent nonnegative valuations are exactly 1,3,...,r−2, so the normalization quotient length is (r−1)/2 and conductor exponent r−1. Hence delta differs by exactly one and conductor by exactly two, with tame m=3 regular. Since z^{m−1} is integral over (x,y) via T²−(xy)z^{m−2}=0 whose coefficient lies in (x,y)², both ideals have equal normalizations of all Rees powers and normalized blowups. Independently checked semigroup gaps and conductor thresholds for odd m through 301; universal proof is the explicit Rees algebra and semigroup argument.
